summary: Acting commander Erin Deka retains Thunderbreak after Venn's tribunal removal; she accepts third-window Fleet screen orders and positions the cruiser to protect civilians while its offensive weapons remain under Admiralty release.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Third-window screen orders received. Offensive weapons remain under Admiralty release.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Commodore Venn's tribunal finding?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Unchanged. Thunderbreak remains under your command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire has the departure mouth. Sunlash holds the far exit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Bring our shields around their route. Leave the guns dark.

panelPlan: On Thunderbreak's familiar, repaired command deck, Lieutenant Deka takes the chair and receives the standing third-window screen orders. Venn is not aboard and her tribunal removal has not been rescinded.
The tactical officer confirms that Deka retains shipboard command while Admiralty separately retains offensive-weapon release. No temporary commission for Venn exists.

Deka compares Gravefire's Shard departure-mouth station with Sunlash's Verge receiving station; these independent captains control their own vessels and know their own routes, not Thunderbreak's internal systems.

Deka commands Thunderbreak's crew to rotate the heavy cruiser's shield sector toward the planned civilian crossing. Its offensive guns stay dark; this is Deka's decision under her standing Fleet authority.
directionInline: Continuity from RF_I02_P18 and RF_I03_P25–P28: Deka is Thunderbreak's duly appointed acting commander after Venn's authenticated relief. Venn remains removed by tribunal, absent from this bridge and unable to direct the ship. No emergency field commission restores her.

Naomi and Tess remain aboard Sunlash and Gravefire, respectively. Neither selects Thunderbreak's captain, touches its controls, or knows its ship-specific procedures. Their route positions are shared over conventional ship-to-ship channels.
Thunderbreak is the same older repaired Fleet heavy cruiser with prior armor and tractor strain; shield geometry and inactive weapons must be physically coherent.

summary: Dominion confirms Deka's existing command of Thunderbreak and limits its third-window blockade role; Deka warns that rescuing a drifting civilian craft may require a defensive deviation from the authorized screen.
settingText: INT. BASTION SPIRE — RELIC COURT / INT. THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND (COMMS FEED)

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Lieutenant Deka, the ship remains yours. The civilian compact does not change Fleet command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Your third-window screen is approved. Offensive weapons remain under Admiralty release.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: A disabled skiff won't stay neatly inside your boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then protect the crossing without abandoning the blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: I'll hold the civilians. You'll have to decide what that costs us.

panelPlan: Dominion at the Relic Court studies the Tal Corvus crossing beside a Fleet blockade map; Deka is visible only on a secure ship-to-ship Fleet communications feed.
Dominion confirms Deka's continuing command and issues narrow operational constraints. Naomi and Tess have no say in appointing or replacing Thunderbreak's commander.
On Thunderbreak, Deka checks a plausible disabled-skiff trajectory against the existing shield and blockade geometry; the risk is a real maneuvering problem, not speculative magic.
The call ends without agreement on how to handle a rescue outside the assigned sector. Deka stays at her own command station; the weapons station remains unarmed pending Admiralty release.
directionInline: Deka, not Venn, receives Dominion's orders in the active Fleet chain of command. Dominion does not restore Venn, and no Verge or Shard captain may appoint or veto a Fleet commander.
Make the central conflict about a Fleet commander's responsibility when a civilian rescue conflicts with a rigid blockade line. Keep Dominion's lawful concerns operationally credible.

summary: Deka identifies how the three hostile screens intend to pry apart the independent rescue escorts and warns Pike that his camera-oriented position obstructs the Fleet reserve approach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: One screen has Gravefire. One has Sunlash. The third is waiting for our reserve to move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: They only have to pull us apart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Broken Oath is blocking the reserve's turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Tell Pike there's a civilian tug behind his cameras.

panelPlan: Thunderbreak's bridge: Tactical shows the three independent hostile intercept vectors, with Deka at her own command station.
Deka recognizes the gap that would open if either allied escort abandoned the civilians to pursue its challenger.
Broken Oath crosses the Fleet reserve's available rescue approach while its cameras point toward the impending crossing.
Deka sends Pike a warning by open channel but retains control of Thunderbreak and keeps its offensive guns inactive.
directionInline: No change in Thunderbreak command since RF_I04_P04: Deka orders the Fleet crew; Tess and Naomi maneuver only their respective Shard and Verge craft.
Render the three-screen geometry as comprehensible ship movement, not abstract supernatural imagery.

summary: Tess and Deka coordinate practical mutual cover across separate Shard and Fleet vessels as Gravefire guides civilians to the departure mouth; neither yields command of her own ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's making the mouth too tight. I can bring them out, but not turn them twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: I'll give you Thunderbreak's armored side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Keep your guns away from their noses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: They stay dark. Take the shelter while it's there.

panelPlan: On Gravefire's bridge Tess guides the staged civilian skiffs away from Ashfang's crowded approach, keeping the launch geometry steady.
Cut to Thunderbreak's command deck: Deka, not Venn, orders a slow cruiser rotation to interpose its established armored and shielded flank.
A single coherent exterior view shows the independent Shard cutter and Fleet heavy cruiser protecting the same narrow departure course without changing ownership or command.
Back aboard Gravefire, Tess acknowledges the usable shelter by continuing to guide the civilian skiffs. The first active transit marker has not yet lit.
directionInline: Tess is aboard Gravefire and Deka aboard Thunderbreak. Their exchange is conventional ship-to-ship operational coordination, not a shipboard visit or shared command. Tess does not know Thunderbreak's controls or determine its captain.
Maintain the distrust between Shard and Fleet without presenting either captain as morally or operationally subordinate. No retroactive familiarity between Tess and Thunderbreak.

summary: Deka obeys the prohibition on offensive fire but commits Thunderbreak's armored flank and shields to protecting two scattered civilian tugs, narrowing her defensive margin.
panelPlan: On Thunderbreak's bridge the Fleet gunner offers Deka a weapons-control option while the two tug tracks peel away from the protected lane.
Deka refuses to seek an unauthorized offensive shot and orders Helm to rotate the cruiser toward the civilian tracks instead.
The established older heavy cruiser brings its broad repaired armor and shield geometry between the tugs and the hostile rim, with the guns dark and the maneuver's cost visible.
From inside the shield shadow, both drifting tugs remain exposed on opposite sides, so the rescue problem is not yet solved.
directionInline: Deka is the acting commander making the defensive decision and accepting responsibility. Venn is not on this bridge and does not authorize either weapons or maneuver.
Respect Dominion's offensive-weapon release condition. The shield movement is physically coherent with Thunderbreak's accumulated damage and finite response time.

summary: A junior Fleet escort officer independently breaks formation to rescue the second drifting tug; Thunderbreak commander Deka chooses to cover that unauthorized rescue despite the resulting breach in the blockade screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: The second tug's beyond the reserve edge. It won't make it back under its own power.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Standing order is to hold the Fleet screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: I'm going after it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: You just opened our flank. I'll cover it. Get them aboard.

panelPlan: The second tug drifts toward the Fleet-side edge, out of time and beyond the assigned escort station.
The junior Fleet escort officer identifies a rescue path and elects to disobey the standing hold order on their own authority.
The smaller Fleet escort turns away from its station before Deka responds, leaving a real opening in the blockade.
On Thunderbreak, Deka sees the exposed gap and orders shields shifted to cover the officer's independent rescue rather than call the ship back.
Exterior: the smaller Fleet craft reaches the tug under fire while Thunderbreak's damaged cruiser hull holds the widened flank.
directionInline: Preserve causal ownership: the junior officer initiates the unauthorized turn before Deka intervenes. Deka makes her own consequential command decision to cover the rescue under active Fleet authority.
Neither Naomi, Tess nor Venn orders Thunderbreak's turn. Deka owns the tactical risk and its disciplinary consequences.

summary: Dominion confronts a Fleet escort's unauthorized formation breach and Deka's independent decision to cover the rescue; Selene insists that the evidence record include the endangered civilians and the lives saved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: That escort left its station without authority. The reserve flank was open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: And a drifting tug was outside its protection.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: If the next ship follows, who guards the civilian convoy?

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: Deka moved Thunderbreak into the gap. Both crews accepted the danger.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: The breach belongs in the record.

dialogueInline.speaker: Selene
dialogueInline.text: So do the people it brought back.

panelPlan: At the Relic Court, Dominion and Selene examine time-ordered war footage showing the junior escort leaving its assigned Fleet station.
Dominion isolates the exposed formation gap while a hostile screen approaches, showing why the breach carries real strategic risk.
Selene advances the record to Deka's Thunderbreak covering that gap and the smaller Fleet escort physically recovering the civilian tug.
The record holds both the unauthorized action and the saved passengers. Institutional judgment of Deka and the junior officer remains unresolved.
directionInline: The tribunal already removed Venn before Issue 4. The officer currently answerable for Thunderbreak's defensive movement is Deka, not Venn. Dominion's disciplinary scrutiny addresses Deka and the junior escort officer.
Selene analyzes historical evidence and named human consequences, not mystical archives. Keep Fleet military and civilian perspectives distinct.
